style: set the scene in one or two plain sentences

candidates.angle: Amanitvam, absence of pride, is the first mark of knowledge
Ahamkara, ego, is absent in this list of virtues
Shama, steadiness and self-control, end the list of qualities

angle_en: Amanitvam: emptying the self of pride
angle_hi: अमानित्व: अहंकार से खुद को खाली करना

en.intro: Krishna finishes his list of what shapes the wise. The qualities are not about grand visions, but about daily conduct.
en.notice: The list opens with amanitvam, the absence of pride, and adamantvam, the absence of pretence. Knowledge begins not with seeing, but with emptying the self of arrogance and show.
en.next: Krishna now turns to the inner eye, describing dispassion toward sense objects and the constant seeing of the fault in birth and death.
en.meaning: Absence of pride, absence of pretence, nonviolence, forgiveness, simplicity, service to the teacher, purity, steadiness, and self-control.

hi.meaning: मानित्व अपने में श्रेष्ठता के भाव का न होना, दम्भित्व दिखावटीपन का न होना, अहिंसा, क्षमा, सरलता, गुरु की सेवा, बाहर-भीतर की शुद्धि, स्थिरता और मन का वश में होना ॥
hi.next: अब कृष्ण अंतर्निरीक्षण की ओर मुड़ते हैं, इंद्रिय विषयों से वैराग्य और जन्म-मृत्यु में दोष देखने का वर्णन करते हैं।

issues: borrowed: "The list opens with amanitvam, the absence of pride, and adamantvam, the absence of pretence." (This swaps the Sanskrit terms. The correct terms are 'amanitvam' (absence of pride) and 'adambhitvam' (absence of pretence). 'Adambhitvam' is misrendered as 'adamantvam', and the explanation for 'amanitvam' is swapped with the explanation for 'adambhitvam'.)
